correctness.rationale: Every maximal geodesic of the four-cube flips all four coordinates once and is hence exactly one of 192 explicit five-vertex masks. Exhausting all 65536 vertex-subset masks gives exact feasible and minimal polynomials. Complete bit-toggle adjacency is exactly legal single addition/removal. Four bounded-state graphs have verified component-size multisets, and BFS over all 3250 connected budget-eight states from each minimum gives the 780-pair distance profile. Primary shortest-path permutation enumeration and independent adjacency-distance DFS agree; BFS and union-find component methods agree. Both embedded Python programs ran to their terminal success assertions. These finite enumerations are exhaustive, not extrapolations.

New determinations are the complete inclusion-minimal distribution, all components and precise budget thresholds for unit addition/removal, and all 780 optimal pair distances at budget eight. The near-exact earlier four-cube result contains no implication of these dynamic or seven/eight-cardinality conclusions; primary papers cover scalar optimization or different path-cover requirements. Unindexed priority remains a nonzero risk.

value.rationale: The four-cube is a canonical finite shortest-path network whose 40 optimum geodesic-hitting placements were already classified. The genuinely new object is their permissible relocation space with a bounded number of temporary sensors, a natural planning/monitoring question. Exactly two spare sensors connect every optimum but three connect the whole feasible family; 160 seven-set and 260 eight-set minimal obstructions provide the reason for an initially increasing component count, while the exact twelve-move maximum quantifies routing costs. This is a motivated complete finite reconfiguration classification rather than an isolated uncontextualized count.
